title: The Inverse Polynomial over a Commutative Ring
content: The construction that carries the parent's field result into an arbitrary commutative ring. `invPoly A := C (Ring.inverse (−c₀)) · divX (charpoly A)`, where `c₀ = (charpoly A).coeff 0`. The single change from the field version is that the scalar reciprocal `(−c₀)⁻¹` is replaced by the ring inverse `Ring.inverse (−c₀)`, which is a genuine inverse exactly when `−c₀` is a unit. Everything downstream is the claim that evaluating this explicit polynomial at `A` returns `A⁻¹` whenever `det A` is a unit. It is `noncomputable` only because it references `Ring.inverse` and the characteristic polynomial.
mathContext: $r = C(\mathrm{Ring.inverse}(-c_0))\cdot \mathrm{div}_X(p)$ with $p = \mathrm{charpoly}\,A$; $\deg r < \deg p = n$ and $(\mathrm{aeval}\,A)\,r = A^{-1}$ once $\det A$ is a unit.

title: Invertibility Forces a Unit Constant Term
content: `isUnit_neg_charpoly_coeff_zero` is the arithmetic heart of the upgrade. Over a field one only needs `c₀ ≠ 0`; over a commutative ring one needs `−c₀` to be an actual unit. The proof uses `Matrix.det_eq_sign_charpoly_coeff` to write `det A = (−1)ⁿ · c₀`, then observes `(−1)ⁿ` squares to `1` so it is a self-inverse unit. Hence `IsUnit (det A)` transfers to `IsUnit c₀`, and negation preserves units, giving `IsUnit (−c₀)`. This is precisely the hypothesis under which `Ring.inverse (−c₀)` behaves like a reciprocal.
relatedConcepts: Determinant and the characteristic polynomial constant term
IsUnit closure under products and negation

title: Cayley–Hamilton in Additive Form
content: `aeval_divX_mul_self` peels the constant term off the characteristic polynomial. Starting from `Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly` (Cayley–Hamilton: `p(A) = 0`) and the identity `divX p · X + C (p.coeff 0) = p` (`divX_mul_X_add`), evaluating at `A` and distributing `aeval` over the sum and product yields `(divX p)(A)·A + c₀•1 = 0`. This is the relation `(polynomial in A)·A = scalar` that, after dividing by the unit `−c₀`, exhibits the inverse. It holds over any commutative ring with no invertibility hypothesis.
mathContext: $(\mathrm{aeval}\,A)(\mathrm{div}_X p)\cdot A + c_0\bullet 1 = 0$, obtained by evaluating $p = \mathrm{div}_X p\cdot X + C\,c_0$ at $A$ using $p(A)=0$.
relatedConcepts: Splitting off the constant term via divX

title: The Inverse as a Polynomial in A
content: The core cluster. `aeval_invPoly_mul_self` divides the additive relation by the unit `−c₀`: where the field proof used `(−c₀)⁻¹·(−c₀) = 1`, here `Ring.inverse_mul_cancel _ hunit` does the same on the unit `−c₀`, producing `(aeval A)(invPoly A) · A = 1`. `inv_eq_aeval_invPoly` promotes this left inverse to the nonsingular inverse via `Matrix.inv_eq_left_inv`, giving `A⁻¹ = (aeval A)(invPoly A)`. `invPoly_natDegree_lt` bounds the degree below `n` from `natDegree_C_mul_le`, `degree_divX_lt`, and `charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim`. `inv_mem_adjoin` then places `A⁻¹` in `Algebra.adjoin R {A} = R[A]` using `Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval`, and `self_mul_aeval_invPoly` records the right-inverse companion via `Matrix.mul_eq_one_comm`.
mathContext: $A^{-1} = (\mathrm{aeval}\,A)(\mathrm{invPoly}\,A) = \mathrm{Ring.inverse}(-c_0)\bullet (\mathrm{div}_X p)(A)$, of degree $< n$, and $A^{-1}\in R[A]$.

title: Packaged Existence, Adjugate Reconciliation and the GL(n, ℤ) Instance
content: The closing results tie the construction to the rest of Mathlib and demonstrate its reach beyond fields. `exists_inv_eq_aeval` packages the main result as a degree-bounded existence statement `∃ r, r.natDegree < n ∧ A⁻¹ = (aeval A) r`. `inv_eq_smul_adjugate` shows the polynomial inverse is the same matrix as Mathlib's adjugate inverse `Ring.inverse (det A) • adjugate A` (`Matrix.inv_def`), so the two constructions describe one and the same `A⁻¹`. Finally the `example` over `ℤ` — not a field — exhibits a unimodular integer matrix (`det A = ±1`) whose inverse lies in the integer-coefficient subalgebra `ℤ[A]`, the concrete case out of reach of the field-only parent.
